title: Low-Temperature Holographic Conductivity
authors: Sabyasachi Maulik, Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas, Jingchao Zhang
abstract: We revisit holographic electrical conductivity in the regime of very low temperatures where quantum fluctuations in the throat of the near-extremal, asymptotically AdS$_4$ dual black brane are strongly coupled. We treat the fluctuations via an effective two-dimensional action capturing the effects of the Schwarzian modes at the scale $1/C$. Our main result is a non-monotonic temperature dependence: the quantum-corrected conductivity decreases as the temperature is lowered, reaches a minimum at $(CT_{\mathrm{min}}\simeq 0.023)$, and grows as $(1/\sqrt{CT})$ for $(CT\ll 1)$. We further estimate the one-loop contribution to the conductivity directly from the four-dimensional gravitational path integral and find qualitative agreement with the effective two-dimensional description in the regime $(CT\gg 1)$. We find that quantum corrections substantially modify the low-temperature behavior of the holographic conductivity in both approaches.
summary: This paper calculates how quantum effects modify the electrical conductivity of a black brane at very low temperatures using holographic methods. It derives a non-monotonic temperature dependence for this conductivity by comparing results from an effective 2D action against direct one-loop gravitational calculations. The findings highlight that quantum corrections significantly alter the expected low-temperature behavior.
main_problem: The study revisits holographic electrical conductivity at very low temperatures where quantum fluctuations near a black brane throat are strongly coupled.
main_result: The quantum-corrected conductivity exhibits a non-monotonic temperature dependence, decreasing to a minimum before growing as $1/\sqrt{CT}$ in the deep low-temperature limit.
method: The authors employ two complementary theoretical approaches: using an effective two-dimensional action capturing Schwarzian modes, and calculating the one-loop contribution directly from the four-dimensional gravitational path integral.
model_or_system: The model involves a near-extremal Reissner-Nordström (RN) black brane in AdS$_4$ spacetime, analyzed via holographic methods derived from the AdS/CFT correspondence.
key_observables: Holographic electrical conductivity ($\sigma_{DC}$), quantum corrections to transport coefficients.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and the dimensionless parameter $CT$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating quantum fluctuations via effective 2D actions or performing one-loop calculations in the gravitational path integral, assuming validity in specific temperature regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 6 shows a function $g_T(k)$ with a maximum increasing rapidly with $T$; Figure 8 compares the two-dimensional Wightman function numerically to analytical estimates.
paper_structure: The paper reviews standard DC conductivity calculations using linearized fluctuations, then develops and compares results from an effective 2D Schwarzian mode action against direct 4D gravitational path integral methods for quantum corrections.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity/condensed matter duality, the analysis of strongly coupled low-temperature transport coefficients and quantum corrections mirrors problems in strongly correlated electron systems where thermal fluctuations are suppressed.
